pages.name: Double the field
pages.task: With nothing connected, the field current doubles from 100% to 200%. The curve marks 440 V at 100% and 555 V at 200%. How many times higher is the voltage now?
pages.why: 555 ÷ 440 = 1.26. The field current doubled, but the flux did not. The iron is saturating, so the voltage rose by only 26%.

pages.name: The exciter
pages.text: In a brushless set, the automatic voltage regulator, or AVR, feeds the exciter's fixed field. The exciter's turning coils make AC. A diode bridge on the shaft turns it into DC for the main field. No brushes are needed.

pages.name: What the AVR feeds
pages.task: In a brushless set, which winding does the AVR's output feed?
pages.why: The AVR sits off the shaft. It feeds the exciter's fixed field, which needs no brushes. The exciter's turning coils and the diodes then carry a much bigger current into the main field.

pages.name: Through a short circuit
pages.task: A short circuit on the board pulls the set's output voltage close to zero. Which AVR supply can keep the field up?
pages.why: The PMG takes its power from the shaft, not from the output. So the AVR can keep the exciter's field up through the fault. A shunt-fed AVR loses its power with the output. So the field and the fault current die away. The protection needs that current to last long enough to clear the fault.

pages.name: The load trips
pages.task: The AVR holds 440 V at 50% load, so the field sits at 125%. The load trips off. The curve marks 490 V at 125%. What is the voltage in the instant before the AVR acts?
pages.why: The field is still at 125%, so the curve gives 490 V inside. With no load there is no drop. So the output jumps to 490 V. Then the AVR lowers the field until the board reads 440 V again.

pages.name: A light load
pages.task: The AVR is on and the load rises from 0% to 20%. The drop is 1 V for each 1% of load. The curve runs straight from 440 V at 100% to 490 V at 125%. What field current does the AVR settle at?
pages.why: The drop is 20 V, so the set must make 460 V inside. That is 20 V of the 50 V between 100% and 125%. So the field rises 20 ÷ 50 × 25 = 10%, to 110%.

pages.alt: A brushless generator set drawn side-on along one shaft turning at 1800 rev/min: the PMG, the exciter with its fixed field and turning coils, the diodes on the shaft, and the main field inside the stator. The output runs to the load. The AVR is on. It senses the output, takes its power from the output, by the shunt lead, and feeds the exciter's fixed field. The exciter's field bars and the main field's bar stand past their 100% ticks.
